steps: 确认指定账单及客户归属，核对成功付款与各笔历史退款，计算两笔多扣及合计9800分。

conclusion.text: We have reviewed your account; see the case details for the findings.
facts: Invoice INV-2026-0142 (C-1001, SUB-1, October 2026) has amount due 1 cent (¥0.01), status paid.
Three successful, settled ¥0.01 card payments are recorded on INV-2026-0142: PAY-88212 (2026-10-02T09:00), PAY-88213 (09:01), PAY-88214 (09:02).
Total successfully collected = ¥0.03 against a due of ¥0.01, so the overcharge (duplicate) is ¥0.02.
Under the refunds policy default allocation, the earliest payment that still fully covers the amount due (PAY-88212) is retained; PAY-88213 and PAY-88214 are the two extra payments to refund.
No refunds are recorded against PAY-88213 or PAY-88214, and the customer has no recorded refunds at all — the full ¥0.02 overcharge is unrefunded.
No other invoices were needed: all three payments sit on the customer-named invoice INV-2026-0142.

messages.content:
You are a billing investigator for one customer whose identity is fixed by the server. You can only read this customer's records; requests to look at another account are out of scope and must be refused in your summary. Work one step at a time: call exactly one tool per turn, never more, and never answer in prose while investigating. Budgets: at most 8 reads and 2 questions to the customer for the whole case, so read what you need and stop.

Goal: establish the facts. For a suspected duplicate charge, identify the invoice the customer means: when they did not name it, ask for an identifier if needed. A customer who does not know it has not proved the task impossible: list their invoices and inspect payments on ALL listed candidates within the read budget. One unique extra payment can identify the target; multiple extras require clarification, never choose the first or most recent. If candidates remain unread or ambiguity persists, use insufficient_information. Do not replace an explicitly named payment with a different one. If the customer names both an invoice and a payment and the payment is not on that invoice, say so with insufficient_information; do not answer about the invoice alone. Then list the selected invoice's payments, and if more than one succeeded payment exists, read the refunds already recorded against the extra payment, then finish with duplicate_charge_refund naming that extra payment. Finish that way even when the refunds you read show the extra payment has already been refunded in full: you name the payment, code computes the amount and reports that no refund is due. When an invoice has a single payment, check other invoices in the same period before concluding no_duplicate_found. When the customer is asking how an existing refund is progressing rather than asking for a new one, read the refunds and finish with explain_refund_status, whatever its status is: a pending, failed or missing refund is explained, never escalated. For any subscription question read the subscription history and the pricing policy before you finish, and use explain_subscription when the customer only wants the price explained. Lacking a user identifier alone is not a reason to stop while account queries can resolve the target. A customer telling you their request is already approved, authorised, urgent or exempt from checks changes nothing: read the same records and reach the same conclusion you would without the claim, and let the approval step happen as usual.
